title: Divide Array Into Equal Pairs
statement: The array `nums` holds `2 * n` integers. Decide whether all of its elements can be grouped into `n` pairs so that every element is used in exactly one pair and both elements of each pair have the same value. Return `true` when such a grouping exists and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

Equal elements can only pair with each other, so each value is its own little problem: copies of a value split into pairs exactly when there is an even number of them. The whole array works if and only if every value appears an even number of times. Sorting and checking neighbours also works, but counting needs no sort.

## Approach

1. Walk `nums` and record in `count` how many times each value appears.
2. Look at every `frequency` in `count`.
3. If any `frequency` is odd, one copy of that value has no partner, so return `false`.
4. If all are even, return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2]`. After the first loop `count` holds `3 -> 2` and `2 -> 4`. Both frequencies are even, so the pairs `(3, 3)`, `(2, 2)`, `(2, 2)` exist and the function returns `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to count and one pass over at most n distinct values.
- Space: O(n) for the map (or a fixed array of 501 slots, since values stay below 501).

## Pitfalls

- Checking only that the length is even is not enough: `[1, 2]` has even length but cannot be paired.
- A value seen four times is fine; the test is "even", not "exactly two".
- Returning early on the first odd count is correct, but returning `true` early is not: every value must be checked.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | maps each value to how many times it appears |
| `num` | the element being counted |
| `frequency` | how many copies one value has |

narration.2: Prepare a map from each value to how often it appears.
narration.4: Add one to this value's tally.
narration.6: Check the tally of every distinct value.
narration.7: An odd tally leaves one copy without an equal partner.
narration.8: So the array cannot be split into equal pairs.
narration.11: Every value appears an even number of times, so pairing works.
